# Sirach Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_004_page_001.jpg

---

1 My child, don't deprive the poor of what they need to live. Don't keep desperate people waiting and hoping in vain.

2 Don't add to the misery of someone who is starving. Don't provoke someone who is already at the end of their rope.

3 Don't pour salt into a bitter wound. Don't delay giving when someone is in need.

4 Don't turn away a plea from someone in distress. Don't refuse to look at the poor.

5 Don't ignore the needy — you don't want anyone cursing your name.

6 If a person curses you out of anguish, their Creator will hear that prayer.

7 Win the respect of your community. Show proper deference to those with authority.

8 Give the poor a hearing. Answer them with gentleness and humility.

9 Rescue victims from their oppressors. Don't lose your nerve when a judgment needs to be rendered.

10 Be a father to the fatherless, a husband's protector to widows — and you will be like a child of the Most High. He will love you even more than a mother loves her own child.

11 Wisdom is a mother to her children; she comes to the aid of all who pursue her.

12 To love Wisdom is to love life itself. Those who seek her out early will overflow with joy.

13 Whoever clings to her will be crowned with honor, and God will bless every house she enters.

14 Those who serve Wisdom serve the Holy One — God loves everyone who loves her.

15 Those who obey her will have the discernment to judge nations; those who listen to her will live securely.

16 Trust Wisdom fully, and she becomes your inheritance; your children after you will possess her.

17 But she doesn't make it easy at first. She leads her students along steep and winding roads. She makes them anxious and afraid. She disciplines them rigorously — until she is satisfied they can be trusted.

18 Then she turns around and leads them back on the smooth path. She restores their joy and opens up her deepest secrets to them.

19 But if they wander away from her, she lets them go — and hands them over to whatever destroys them.

20 Watch your timing. Steer clear of evil. And don't be ashamed of who you are.

21 Some kinds of shame lead straight to sin. Other kinds of shame lead to honor and grace.

22 Don't compromise yourself by playing favorites. Don't let fear of the powerful become your downfall.

23 Speak up when the moment calls for it. Don't sit on your wisdom.

24 Words are how wisdom makes itself known; teaching flows through what the tongue says.

25 Don't argue against truth. Be honest about what you don't know.

26 Don't be too proud to admit your sins. Don't try to swim against an impossible current.

27 Don't put yourself under a fool's authority. Don't go out of your way to please the powerful.

28 Fight for what is true, all the way to your last breath — and God himself will fight alongside you.

29 Don't be careless with your words or lazy with your actions.

30 Don't be a tyrant in your own home. Don't treat your own household like suspects.

31 Don't be the kind of person whose hand is always out to receive but never open to give.
